audit.whatIsWrong: Three chart rows contradicted their own why-strings, and the difficulty label contradicts the data. phases[4] gave level 6 to Swain while whys[4] says Kled's R rams him out of E range; phases[6] gave 2+ items to Kled while whys[6] says 'Two-item Swain reclaims the lane'; row 1 was Skill while whys[1] is Kled-positive. Separately the lane is marked TRICKY at 7.5/10 while winning 57.66% over 222 games with Kled holding 5 of 7 stages.
audit.why: Swain is immobile: Kled's level-6 charge and his 2-3 window are real edges, and the row that genuinely belongs to Swain is the two-item drain timing the text already describes.
audit.corrected: Rows 1, 4 and 6 flipped as paired full+content rows to give Swain/Kled/Kled/Kled/Kled/Kled/Swain — the packet chart. diff -> EVEN, tone -> the even colour, diffRating -> 5.5/10, with breakdown.difficulty and report[14] updated to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text credited Kled's Bear Trap with percent-HP damage, and Demonic Ascension was described only as 'his drain'.
audit.why: Kled Q carries no percentHealth flag. Demonic Ascension is 120s flat at every rank, 650 range, and Riot's text says the form is indefinite AS LONG AS he keeps draining enemy champions — so stepping out of 650 range ends it, which is a usable instruction rather than a warning.
audit.corrected: Percent-HP claims removed; the 120s/650-range/keeps-draining rule now appears in mid, breakdown.cooldowns and dosFull[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags that none of Swain's abilities are ever named, and the decisive property of Nevermove was never stated.
audit.why: Nevermove (E, 12s at rank 1, 850 range) launches a wave forward and roots only when it RETURNS to Swain — the wave passing over you on the way out does nothing. Sidestepping the return is the entire counterplay and it was absent from every field.
audit.corrected: The return-trip root now appears in early, wants.you[0], report[5], dontsFull[1] and breakdown.cooldowns; Death's Hand, Vision of Empire, Nevermove, Ravenous Flock and Demonic Ascension are all named on the correct slots.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both missing-interaction entries were unstated in prose: Swain sustains through chip via Ravenous Flock, and he invalidates stacked resistances.
audit.why: Soul Fragments heal him AND permanently raise his maximum health, so armour/MR alone never closes the gap — Grievous Wounds timing is what decides an extended trade. report[8] already buys Executioner's Calling but no prose field explained why.
audit.corrected: Anti-heal reasoning added to whys[6], mid and late.

edits.before: Swain concedes nothing at Level 1 — his Q poke and E pull mean you should respect his range until W comes online. The whole early game is his E: if he lands that line pull he roots you and chains W bomb and Q for a big chunk of Skaarl's health, so weave through minions and never walk in a straight line at him. The instant you hit Level 2-3 with W (the on-hit shotgun shots) and your full E-W-E re-E, you all-in — he has no dash, so once you E through and recast back he cannot escape your burst.
edits.after: Swain concedes nothing at Level 1 — Death's Hand poke and an 850-range Nevermove mean you respect his range until W comes online. The whole early game is that E: the wave roots on the way BACK, not on the way out, so once it passes you, step sideways and the return whiffs. Rooted, he chains Vision of Empire and Q for a chunk of Skaarl. The instant you hit Level 2-3 with Violent Tendencies and the full E-W-E re-E, all-in — no dash means he cannot escape the recast.

edits.before: This is your lane. Keep baiting his E — when that pull is on cooldown he is defenseless, so that is your engage signal: E in, W-pull-yank with Q, and stack W procs while your remount sustains the drain. At 6 your R knocks him out of his own E range and turns every all-in lethal, and it doubles as gank-extension to snowball other lanes. Just respect that if he ults (R) in an extended fight his drain heals everything, so kill him fast or back off — never sit in his soul-drain.
edits.after: This is your lane. Keep baiting Nevermove — 12s at rank 1, and with that pull down he is defenceless, so that is your engage signal: E in, Bear Trap yank, and stack the W attacks while remount sustain covers his chip. At 6 your R rams him out of his own 850-range E and doubles as gank-extension to snowball other lanes. Respect one thing: Demonic Ascension lasts as long as he keeps draining a champion, so burst him with Grievous Wounds up or leave the 650 range.

edits.before: You own the straight 1v1 through your first item, but Swain is a scaling drain monster and this is where it flips. Past two items his E-root into full R drain and W bomb out-sustain your frontloaded burst, and in any teamfight his AOE drain heals through your damage while your team eats his root. Close the lane and take his tower before ~25 minutes — if the game goes long he becomes a fight he wins, so cash in your early leads with R roams while you still own the map.
edits.after: You own the straight 1v1 through your first item, but Swain is a scaling drain monster and this is where it flips. Past two items Nevermove into a full Demonic Ascension out-heals your frontloaded burst, and Ravenous Flock's fragments keep raising his maximum health, so armour and MR alone never solve him — Grievous Wounds does. Close the lane and take his tower early, and cash your leads with R roams while you still own the map.
